units.title: Live Done-when pass for evolution and breeding on 46630
units.description: Runs the epic's Done when end to end on the final 46630 deployment and the Vercel app as a scripted checklist, with stage levels lowered through the Safe and timelock for the drill and restored to 3, 6, 15 and 30 after: a pet grows Baby → Teen with its path → Adult and its element look shows on the Home stage; one reaches Elder with a bought item and one reaches Mythic with a Mythic item and a season trophy won in a shortened test season; an own-pets breed and a Co-Pet breed with both approvals at the doubling cost; each breed's egg, shiny flag included, is recomputed from its revealed seed with entry 2's breedOutcome; the Evolve and Breed sheets show every state in EXPERIENCE.md's spine.

acceptance.clause: The checklist's tx hashes on 46630 and Vercel screenshots show every Done when item passing, the restored stage levels read 3, 6, 15 and 30 from the contract views, and the owner signs it off.

units.title: Tracer: a robbery reaches the Home alert pill and a desktop web push
units.description: Delivers CAP-27's thinnest path through every layer: a notifier job in the worker loop turns each PetRobbed row the indexer writes to BattleRecord (6.1) into one Notification row (Prisma models Notification with a string kind, not an enum, so later kinds need no migration, and a unique dedupeKey, writer = notifier, and PushSubscription, writer = API), a message-template module (kind → title, body, action label and app link) and a Channel port with the web-push adapter (`web-push`, approved in DECISIONS #24, VAPID subject an https URL, no email) that later entries reuse, the one deep-link format `/<screen>?alert=<id>` that push, Telegram (entry 2) and the pill (entry 9) all use, a service worker in the app that shows the push and opens the action link, a subscribe/unsubscribe API route, a GET alerts route, and a bare alert pill on Home showing "Biscuit took 624 points from Mochi. Revenge?" (EXPERIENCE copy; push and Telegram use the mock's "Biscuit robbed Mochi: −624 points").
notes: hitl steps: the owner generates the VAPID key pair and enters it in the local env (and later Render and Vercel, entry 12); secrets are never printed (CLAUDE.md).
High risk: outside check = the owner sees the push arrive on their own desktop browser from a staged robbery.

acceptance.clause: With the app, worker and a Hardhat local node running, an attack that robs the test player's pet produces, within a minute, exactly one Notification row, the alert pill on Home naming the attacker and points lost, and one desktop Chrome push with the same text whose tap opens Battle; replaying the same log adds no second row.

units.title: Telegram bot links by one-time token and sends the robbery alert with a button
units.description: Adds the Telegram channel with plain HTTPS Bot API calls (fetch, no bot library): an API route that mints a single-use link token (base64url, at most 64 [A-Za-z0-9_-] characters, short expiry, stored hashed) and returns `t.me/<bot>?start=<token>`, a worker long-polling job on getUpdates that resolves `/start <token>` into a TelegramLink row (chat id, writer = notifier) and confirms, `/stop` to unlink, and a Telegram adapter on entry 1's Channel port that sends the template text with an inline URL button ("Open Petverse" / "Revenge") using entry 1's `/<screen>?alert=<id>` deep link, registered in its own file without editing the template module; the Settings screen (entry 7) mounts the link button.
notes: hitl steps: the owner creates the bot with BotFather (name, username, description) and enters the bot token and username in the local env (later Render and Vercel, entry 12); agents never touch the live bot account (CLAUDE.md).
High risk: outside check = the owner links their own Telegram account and receives the staged robbery.

acceptance.clause: Tests against a recorded-fixture Bot API pass for link, reuse of a spent token (refused), expired token (refused), /stop and send; then, with the worker running against the owner's test bot, the owner opens the link URL from the route on their phone, taps Start, and a staged robbery arrives in Telegram with a button that opens the app on Battle.

units.title: The app installs as a PWA so web push works on iPhone from the Home Screen
units.description: Makes web push reach iOS: a web app manifest (standalone display, name, theme colours from DESIGN.md, 180/192/512 px icons rendered from an existing 3D pet), apple-touch-icon and meta tags, service worker registration that survives install, a check that on iPhone Safari outside the installed app shows "Add Petverse to your Home Screen to get alerts" (assumed copy) instead of a permission request, and a subscribe call made only from a user tap inside the installed app.
notes: hitl steps: the owner OKs the Vercel preview deploy with the VAPID public key set, installs the PWA on their own iPhone (iOS 16.4 or later) and confirms the push; an Android phone check is welcome too.
High risk: outside check = the owner's iPhone receives the push from the installed app.

acceptance.clause: On a Vercel preview, the owner adds Petverse to an iPhone Home Screen, opens it, taps the test subscribe button, and receives a staged robbery push; in iPhone Safari (not installed) the add-to-Home-Screen hint shows and no permission prompt appears; Lighthouse marks the app installable.

units.title: Push permission is asked once, after the first feed
units.description: Adds the permission ask to the feed flow: after the player's first successful feed a bottom sheet explains alerts in one line (assumed copy: "We'll tell you when Mochi is hungry or robbed") with Turn on / Not now, Turn on runs the browser prompt and saves the subscription through entry 1's route, a denied or dismissed prompt is remembered so no prompt repeats, and on iPhone outside the installed app it shows entry 3's hint instead.

acceptance.clause: Component tests show the sheet appears after the first feed and never after the second, Turn on saves one PushSubscription, and a denied browser prompt leaves no subscription and no later sheet.

units.title: Hungry, asleep, close-to-death and passed-away alerts fire at the right moments
units.description: Adds the time-based and death kinds to the notifier: hungry at the start of the last 24h before sleep, asleep at sleepAt, close to passing away 24h before deathAt (assumption), all computed from projected sleepAt with the AD-16 TS status port and deduped by (petId, kind, sleepAt) in entry 1's dedupeKey, plus passed away from the indexed PetBuried event, with Voice and Tone copy and app links ("Feed Mochi", "Feed to wake") in the template module; a feed that moves sleepAt makes the next window's alerts fire again.

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a test_ schema with a fake clock pin each kind firing once at its boundary (hungry at sleepAt − 24h, asleep at sleepAt, close to death at deathAt − 24h, passed away on PetBuried), none for a pet fed in time, and a fresh set after a feed moves sleepAt.

units.title: Co-Pet, claim, wheel and streak events become in-app alerts
units.description: Adds the remaining kinds to the notifier and template module: Co-Pet partner needs to agree (breed, Death Match) and partner left a Co-Pet from indexed events, small-pot payout ready to claim from the indexed epoch post, and daily wheel ready and login streak at risk from projections, each in-app only by default with push and Telegram off until the owner decides (EXPERIENCE Notifications "not decided").

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a test_ schema emit each event or state once and show exactly one in-app Notification per kind for the right player (the other owner for "needs to agree", the remaining owner for "partner left", the pet's owners for claim ready) and no push or Telegram send for these kinds.

units.title: Notification settings: per-type opt-outs, push status and Telegram link
units.description: Builds Avatar menu › Notifications: a NotificationSettings model (writer = API) with one toggle per alert kind applied to push and Telegram, the player's IANA time zone saved from the browser on each app open, the push on/off state with the denied-state copy "Alerts are off in your browser. You can still link Telegram." and steps to turn them on, and entry 2's Link / Unlink Telegram button; no email field exists.

acceptance.clause: API and component tests show toggling a kind persists per player, the time zone saves from a stubbed browser zone, the denied state shows its copy with no re-prompt, and Link Telegram opens the URL from entry 2's route while Unlink removes the TelegramLink.

units.title: Delivery policy: most urgent only, 3 a day, quiet hours and opt-outs
units.description: Adds one policy step before every push and Telegram send: of the alerts due in a tick only the most urgent goes out (the others stay in-app), at most 3 outside alerts per player per local day counted once across push and Telegram, none from 22:00 to 08:00 in the player's saved time zone except close to death, and opted-out kinds never sent, recording each outside send on the Notification (`sentOutsideAt`, which entry 10's delivery log builds on) so the cap can count it; the cap and quiet hours are read from GameConfig rows written by the admin script (AD-18).

acceptance.clause: Worker tests with a fake clock show a robbery plus hungry plus asleep in one tick sends only the top-ranked one, a fourth alert in a local day is held in-app, a 23:00 hungry alert is not sent while a 23:00 close-to-death alert is, and an opted-out kind is never sent.

units.title: Alert pill on Home and Battle: one at a time, acted on, deep links land right
units.description: Grows entry 1's bare pill into the EXPERIENCE component on Home and the top of Battle: one alert at a time newest first, per-kind copy and action (Revenge, Feed, Open Co-Pet, Claim) from the template module, dismissed when acted on through a mark-read route, and push and Telegram deep links opening the same place with the alert marked read.

acceptance.clause: Component tests show only the newest unread alert, its action button per kind, the pill clearing after the action, and a deep link with an alert id opening the right screen with that alert marked read.

units.title: Failed deliveries are retried, logged and never shown as game errors
units.description: Adds a NotificationDelivery log (writer = notifier) per attempt, building on entry 8's `sentOutsideAt`, and retry with backoff for push and Telegram failures, removes a push subscription on 404/410, unlinks a Telegram chat that blocked the bot (403), honours Telegram's 429 retry_after, and keeps every failure out of the player's screens and out of game API responses (AD-19).

acceptance.clause: Worker tests with fake channels show a 500 is retried then logged as failed, a 410 deletes the subscription, a 403 removes the TelegramLink, a 429 waits its retry_after, and no app route returns an error when a channel fails.

units.title: Send-to-team-chat on the same Telegram bot for epic-launch's ops alarms
units.description: Exports a sendToTeamChat(text) function from the Telegram transport that posts to one team group chat id from env, through entry 10's retry and log, which epic-launch's ops alarms call.
notes: hitl steps: the owner creates the team Telegram group, adds the bot, and enters the group's chat id in the local env and Render secrets.

acceptance.clause: A test against the recorded-fixture Bot API posts to the team chat id with retry on failure, and the owner sees a test message from the worker in the team group.

units.title: Alerts run live on testnet across all three channels
units.description: Deploys the notifier, Telegram polling and team-chat function to the Render worker on the game schema and the service worker, settings and pill to Vercel production with VAPID and bot secrets, and runs epic-alerts' Done when on 46630, the timed alerts on epic-pet-life's drill instance (2.11) whose sleep and death timers are shortened.
notes: hitl steps: the owner OKs the Render and Vercel production deploys (CLAUDE.md), enters VAPID keys, bot token and team chat id in Render and Vercel secrets, and checks the alerts on their own phones.
High risk: outside check = the owner and one teammate each receive the robbery alert on push and Telegram.

acceptance.clause: On 46630 a staged robbery produces one alert naming the attacker and points lost in app, by push on the owner's iPhone and Android or desktop, and on Telegram; a pet on the drill instance (2.11) gets hungry, asleep and close-to-death alerts on the same channels; a 23:00 local hungry alert is held; a fourth alert in a day is held; and a repo search finds no email-sending code.

units.description: Cleans up what the epic's plans and deferred review findings list, with scope set when it starts; cleanup only, any pushed-out scope is a new entry.

acceptance.clause: The gate passes and every deferred finding recorded in this epic's plans is closed or moved to a named entry.

units.title: Tracer: a device-sharing farm on a local node is flagged, its pet's claim is held, and the team sees it
units.description: Delivers the thinnest path through every layer of CAP-29: the auth path records a hashed first-party device id per Privy DID in LoginSeen, a worker risk job with a rule registry flags every account in a device cluster at or over the threshold in GameConfig (the table epic-store-pass 5.8 first uses) into RiskFlag, the worker job registration that entries 4, 5, 6 and 11 plug into, one shared risk-status port in src/server/risk (isFlagged(did, at?) answering now or as of a past time, and flagStatus open / confirmed / cleared from RiskFlag and RiskReview) that entries 7, 8, 9 and 11 read, the RISK signer sets PetCore.payoutHold on each of the flagged account's pets so claim reverts until it expires, and the reviewer-only /admin layout and DID guard that entries 9 and 11 reuse, with a /admin/risk page that lists the flag with its evidence; it adds every model this epic needs (LoginSeen, RiskFlag, RiskReview, PayoutHold projection, MetricDaily) in one migration with their single writers named.

acceptance.clause: A worker test on a Hardhat local node and a test_ schema logs in 3 fixture DIDs from one device id, sees all 3 flagged, a claim by one of their pets revert with the hold error, a fourth DID on another device stay unflagged and claim, and the /admin/risk route list the 3 flags for a reviewer DID and return 403 for any other DID.

units.title: Can the worker find each account's funding wallet on 46630, and which funders must be ignored?
units.description: Answers, for the funding-wallet rule of CAP-29, whether the worker can find the first ETH and PETV sender of every player account (7702 embedded wallets and 4337 smart accounts, native transfers that emit no log) on 46630 through RPC tracing or the Blockscout API, how fresh that answer is, and which shared funders (Faucet, team, Safe, curve, pool, bridge) must be on an ignore list so the faucet does not flag every player.

acceptance.clause: A write-up in epic-anti-bot/ shows the funder found for at least 10 known testnet accounts of each wallet mode with the method, lookup latency and the ignore list, recorded as a dated decision in epic-anti-bot.md Notes.

units.title: Payout hold rules: 72-hour expiry, no back-to-back renewal by RISK, Safe renew and clear
units.description: Completes the AD-15 hold on PetCore: a hold set by RISK expires by itself 72 hours later (N9), RISK cannot set a new hold on a pet within 72 hours of its last hold ending, only the Safe can renew or clear a hold early, RISK may lift a hold it set, a hold blocks the whole claim of a Co-Pet (epic-social 8.2's 50/50 claim path) and the pet's EpochDistributor small-pot claim too, the RISK role can call nothing that moves funds, a Safe-only confirmBot(petId) that settles the pet, recycles its owed + pending unclaimed ETH into the main pot through epic-pot 3.2's buried-pet recycle path and zeroes its pot points (DECISIONS #56), and the indexer projects PayoutHoldSet / PayoutHoldLifted into the PayoutHold table that entries 6 (back-to-back window) and 8 read.

acceptance.clause: Contract tests show a claim reverting at 72h minus 1 second and succeeding at 72h, a back-to-back RISK hold reverting and a Safe renewal succeeding, a Safe clear and a RISK lift releasing the claim, a held pet's EpochDistributor claim reverting, every fund-moving function reverting for the RISK key, and the AD-4 balance invariant still holding with holds in the random steps.

units.title: Perfectly regular timing flags an account
units.description: Adds the timing rule to entry 1's registry: over a rolling 24 hours of an account's indexed game actions, at least 30 actions whose gaps have a coefficient of variation under 0.1 flag the account, with the gap statistics stored as the flag's evidence and the thresholds read from GameConfig.

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a test_ schema flag a fixture account acting every 600 ± 5 seconds, do not flag one acting at human-like irregular gaps or one with only 29 regular actions, and store the computed CV on the flag.

units.title: Many accounts funded by one wallet flag every account in the cluster
units.description: Adds the funding-wallet rule to entry 1's registry behind a funder-lookup port with spike 2's adapter for 46630 and a local-node adapter for tests: at least 3 accounts whose first funding came from the same wallet within 30 days are flagged, funders on the spike's ignore list (Faucet, team, Safe, curve, pool) never form a cluster, and the funder address and cluster size are stored as evidence.

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a local node fund 3 fresh accounts from one wallet and see all flagged, fund 3 from the Faucet and see none flagged, and fund 2 from one wallet and see none flagged.

units.title: Hold keeper: every pet of a flagged account stays held while under review
units.description: Extends the worker risk job so every pet of an open-flagged account is held, including pets it hatches or co-owns after the flag, never re-holds a pet inside RISK's 72-hour back-to-back window, and stores holds ending within 12 hours on an open flag as renewal requests on the RiskFlag row (writer = risk job) with a prepared Safe transaction (Protocol Kit, DECISIONS #32) that entry 9 shows to reviewers.

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a local node show a pet hatched by a flagged account held within one job tick, no RISK hold sent inside the back-to-back window, and an expiring hold on an open flag producing one renewal request whose prepared Safe transaction renews the hold when executed by the test Safe.

units.title: Flagged accounts get no gas sponsorship, faucet drip or free-egg voucher
units.description: Makes the gas webhook (fail closed), the faucet voucher route and the free-egg voucher routes (epic-pet-life 2.1, 2.7) refuse any account isFlagged reports, with the standard error shape and a calm player state ("Free actions are paused while we check your account", and "Claims paused for a check · back by <time>" on a held claim) instead of a game error; paid actions stay open.

acceptance.clause: API tests with recorded Alchemy webhook fixtures refuse sponsorship for a flagged DID and approve it for an unflagged one, the faucet and free-egg voucher routes refuse the flagged DID, the claim sheet shows "Claims paused for a check · back by <time>" for a held pet, and the same DID is sponsored and gets vouchers again once its flag is cleared.

units.title: Flagged and held pets are left out of the small-pot snapshot
units.description: Fills epic-pot's epoch-builder exclusion list (3.5) with every pet whose owner or co-owner was flagged at snapshotTs by entry 1's isFlagged(did, snapshotTs) or that holds a payout hold at the snapshot block, before the bottom-half cut, and publishes the excluded petIds with reason "held" (no evidence) in the epoch dataset so the root still rebuilds from the public route; epic-seasons' season-end job reads the same exclusion through entry 1's port.

acceptance.clause: A worker test on a local node and a test_ schema builds an epoch where a flagged pet and a held pet are excluded before the cut and do not move the cut line, and entry 3.6's rebuild script reproduces the posted root from the public dataset.

units.title: Team review: confirm or clear a flag with a recorded reason
units.description: Completes /admin/risk for reviewer DIDs: each flag shows its rules and evidence, linked accounts and pets, hold expiry and entry 6's renewal requests; a reviewer confirms or clears it with a required reason written to RiskReview, a confirm also preparing the Safe transaction that calls entry 3's confirmBot for each of the account's pets (DECISIONS #56), a clear lifts the account's holds through RISK and makes isFlagged false so sponsorship, vouchers and the next snapshot return, and the flag history is kept.

acceptance.clause: API and page tests on a test_ schema show a reviewer clearing a flagged fixture account (RiskReview row with reviewer DID and reason, holds lifted on a local node, isFlagged false), a clear without a reason refused, and a non-reviewer DID refused with 403.

units.title: Seeded-farm suite: every signal flags, every consequence holds, and the existing counters still bite
units.description: Adds one end-to-end test on a local node that seeds a farm sharing a device, a funding wallet and regular timing beside honest players, and checks the whole of CAP-29 Done when 1 and 4: all farm accounts flagged, no sponsorship, no voucher, out of the next small-pot snapshot, claims held, cleared by review and restored; plus contract pins that a farm gains nothing from same-owner or co-owner battles (epic-battle's ban) or from splitting points across pets (the per-owner curve).

acceptance.clause: The seeded-farm test passes on a local node and a test_ schema with zero honest accounts flagged, and fails when any one rule, refusal or exclusion is switched off.

units.title: Daily metrics job stores the four counter-metrics in MetricDaily
units.description: Adds the AD-23 worker metrics job that after 00:30 UTC writes one MetricDaily row per UTC day from projections: bot share of pot ETH paid (main and small-pot claims to accounts entry 1's port reports open or confirmed), top-5%-of-pets share of pot ETH paid over the trailing 7 days, week-1 churn of new players robbed in their first 7 days, and the share of owners whose pet was buried who hatched again within 7 days; plus a reviewer-only /admin/metrics table with each limit marked.

acceptance.clause: A worker test on a test_ schema with fixture claims, flags, PetRobbed, PetBuried (epic-pet-life 2.6) and hatch projections writes the expected four values for a day, re-running the job for that day changes nothing, and /admin/metrics shows the row with the bot share over 10% marked red.

units.title: Anti-bot live on 46630: hold upgrade, RISK role, worker jobs and a drill
units.description: Upgrades PetCore and EpochDistributor with the hold through the Safe-proposed timelock, grants RISK through the timelock, verifies both on Blockscout, regenerates the chain module, runs the risk, hold-keeper and metrics jobs on Render against the game schema and the review pages on Vercel, and runs the drill: a seeded farm is flagged, held and refused sponsorship, a back-to-back RISK hold reverts, the Safe renews and clears, the Safe confirms one seeded bot pet and its unclaimed ETH returns to the main pot, a reviewer clears an account, and a MetricDaily row appears.

acceptance.clause: The drill's tx hashes on 46630 show the hold set, the RISK renewal revert, the Safe renew and clear, and the cleared account's next sponsored action, both contracts show verified source on Blockscout, and the game schema holds the drill's RiskReview row and that day's MetricDaily row.

units.title: Refactor sweep
units.description: Cleans up what the epic's plans and deferred review findings list, with scope set when it starts; cleanup only, any pushed-out scope is a new entry.

acceptance.clause: The gate passes and every deferred finding recorded in this epic's plans is closed or moved to a named entry.

units.title: Tracer: "Check this result" for one battle result, from Randomness events to the sheet on Vercel
units.description: Delivers the thinnest path through every layer the fairness check touches: a public, unauthenticated route that, for one requestId, reads epic-platform's Randomness service (1.16) register and reveal events (commitment, registering tx and time, secret, reveal tx and time) and the module's settle event, recomputes keccak(secret) = commitment and seed = keccak(secret, requestId), and returns match / pending / timed-out; and the DESIGN fairness-check sheet ("Locked in before the fight", "Revealed after", lime "Matches", "Being revealed · nothing for you to do", "See it on the public record" Blockscout link) opened from the battle result card's "Check this result" link, for battle results only.

acceptance.clause: On the Vercel production app on 46630, after one attack the result card's "Check this result" opens a sheet with lock-in and reveal times and "Matches" with a Blockscout link, and a local-node route test with a tampered reveal returns no match.

units.title: Can every random result type be recomputed from its published commitment and reveal alone?
units.description: Answers, for entry 3, which of the nine result types (battle, wheel, dice, wager, monster, expedition, egg, breeding, cosmetic drop) can be recomputed from the revealed seed plus public on-chain inputs — through a pure contract view, the settle event, or only a TS port — and which need a module change, by reading each module's contract and events on 46630.
units.unknown: If a module emits neither the outcome inputs nor a pure outcome view, does the fix go back to that module's epic as a new entry or into this epic (recommended: back to the owning epic)?

acceptance.clause: A write-up in epic-launch/ lists each of the nine result types with its recompute path, the inputs it needs and one recomputed 46630 result that matches the settled outcome, recorded as a dated decision in epic-launch.md Notes.

units.title: "Check this result" works for all nine result types and the claim sheet
units.description: Extends entry 1's route and sheet to recompute the outcome itself (not only the commitment) for every result type by spike 2's paths, places the link on every result surface the spine names plus monster, expedition, egg-hatch, breeding and cosmetic-drop results, takes over epic-pot's claim-sheet link (3.8, which links to the public share views until then) with a PetCore public-view check, and covers the sheet's Loading, Error, Offline and timed-out states (timed-out copy is an assumption, see Notes).

acceptance.clause: Route tests on a Hardhat local node with the full Ignition module recompute and match one settled result of each of the nine types, report a mismatch for a tampered seed and a no-op for a timed-out request, and on 46630 the sheet shows "Matches" for one real result of each type.

units.title: Launch check: every release-1 contract is verified and governed as AD-3 says
units.description: Adds the launch-check script harness (node, read-only, any chainId) and its first check, which walks every address in the generated chain module and confirms Blockscout shows verified source, every proxy's upgrade admin and parameter setter is the TimelockController with the Safe as sole proposer and canceller, the Safe holds PAUSER, each server key holds exactly one role, and PETV has no minter, writing a pass/fail report other checks (5, 14) reuse.

acceptance.clause: Run against a Hardhat local node with the full Ignition module, the check passes, and it fails naming the contract when a planted extra role grant, a non-timelock admin or an unverified address is introduced; run against 46630 it prints a report.

units.title: Launch check: money numbers in the app match public views, and every epoch root rebuilds
units.description: Adds to entry 4's harness a reconciliation check that, for a sample of pets and players, compares the app's API values (points, pot size, pending share, claims from 3.10, burn total and Gold figures from 4.7's route) with the contract views they come from, and runs epic-pot's rebuild script (3.6) over every posted epoch of every stream to recompute root and datasetHash from the public dataset route alone.

acceptance.clause: On a Hardhat local node seeded by its own fixture (pets, a pot flush, a claim, a burn and one posted epoch) the check passes, fails on a planted off-by-one in one API value and on a tampered dataset leaf, and against 46630 it prints a report with every posted root rebuilt.

units.title: How it's fair page
units.description: Builds the Avatar menu › How it's fair page per the spine: commit–reveal explained in plain words with a link to check any recent result, the list of every contract with its Blockscout verified-source link from entry 4's report format, the Safe 2-of-3 and 1-hour timelock with its pending operations (this entry adds the indexer handlers for the timelock CallScheduled, CallExecuted and Cancelled events that list them), the live pot and burn total read from public views dollars first, and how to rebuild an epoch root from the public dataset route, with Empty, Loading, Error and Offline states and no crypto jargon.

acceptance.clause: On the Vercel app on 46630 the page lists every contract in the chain module with a working verified link, shows the Safe threshold and timelock delay read live, and its pot and burn figures equal the contract views.

units.title: Ops alarms reach the team chat
units.description: Adds an alarms job to the worker that evaluates the AD-23 signals, extending epic-platform's health route (1.9) — indexer lag per contract, reveal backlog and late reveals, keeper backlog, each role key's ETH balance, and the Gas Manager policy balance; the late-reveal alert epic-platform 1.16 raises is routed here to team chat, not built twice — against thresholds kept in config, dedupes and re-arms each alarm, and sends it through epic-alerts' send-to-team-chat function, with the worker health route reporting every signal.
units.unknown: How the worker reads the Alchemy Gas Manager policy balance (API, dashboard only, or a proxy such as sponsored-ops spend from our webhook); recommended: an API read if one exists, else spend tracked from the gas webhook against an owner-entered budget.

acceptance.clause: Worker tests on a local node and test_ schema with a faked team-chat sender fire exactly one alarm each for a stalled cursor, a request unrevealed past 10 minutes, an overdue keeper tick and a signer below threshold, and one recovery message when each clears.

units.title: Team ops dashboard linking the counter-metrics page
units.description: Adds a team-only ops page behind the same reviewer gate epic-anti-bot uses for its /admin/metrics page (one admin gate, same refusal), showing every health signal, open and recent alarms and role-key and Gas Manager balances, linking that metrics page rather than rebuilding it, and adds a daily alarm through entry 7 when a counter-metric crosses its limit.

acceptance.clause: Route tests show a non-reviewer login is refused as /admin/metrics refuses it and a reviewer gets the signals; with seeded MetricDaily rows above a limit the alarms job sends one counter-metric alarm through the faked sender.

units.title: Staged alarm drill on 46630 reaches the team
units.description: Deploys the alarms job to the Render worker on the game schema and stages, on 46630, an indexer stall (worker indexer paused), a request left unrevealed (revealer paused for one request) and a low signer balance (threshold raised above a test key's balance), recording that each alarm and its recovery reach the team chat and the dashboard.

acceptance.clause: A drill record in epic-launch/ lists each staged fault with its time, the team-chat message received, the dashboard view and the recovery message, and the revealer catches up with no lost reveal.

units.title: Runbooks: timelock change, upgrade, pause, cancel, key rotation, deploy and alarm response
units.description: Writes the operator runbooks in docs/runbooks/ — Safe-proposed timelocked parameter change and upgrade, pause and unpause, cancel a queued operation or an epoch root, role-key rotation (grant new, revoke old through the timelock, update the host secret), the full Ignition deploy with Blockscout verification and chain-module regeneration, signer and faucet top-ups, and the response to each alarm from entry 7 — each with Safe web UI and Protocol Kit / CLI paths, plus the Protocol Kit helper scripts they call in chain/scripts/, building on epic-platform's Safe path (1.3) and governance deploy (1.15).

acceptance.clause: A local-node test drives the helper scripts through propose → wait → execute, propose → cancel, pause → unpause and a role rotation against the Ignition-deployed timelock and a test Safe, and every runbook step names the exact command or UI action it uses.

units.title: Runbook drill on 46630 by someone other than the author
units.description: Has a team member who did not write the runbooks follow them on 46630: a Safe-proposed parameter change executed after the 1-hour delay, a cancelled operation, a pause and unpause of one module, and a rotation of one role key with its host secret, fixing every runbook step that did not match.

acceptance.clause: A drill record in epic-launch/ lists each runbook step followed with its tx hash on 46630, who ran it, and each runbook correction made, and the launch check from entry 4 passes after the rotation.

units.title: Refactor sweep
units.description: Cleans up what the epic's plans and deferred review findings list, with scope set when it starts; cleanup only, any pushed-out scope is a new entry.

acceptance.clause: The gate passes and every deferred finding recorded in this epic's plans is closed or moved to a named entry.

units.title: Closing end-to-end suite across every epic
units.description: Delivers the scripted part of CAP-28's "every capability works" proof: one suite that deploys the full release-1 Ignition module on a Hardhat local node with the worker on a test_ schema and drives, through the API and the GameWallet test adapter, each epic's Done when that a script can check (login and hatch, care, pot and claim, PETV trade and burn, store and Pass, battles and wagers, cosmetics and market, Co-Pet and guilds, play hub, seasons, growth, alerts, anti-bot holds, fairness check), with a read-only smoke mode that runs the same checks' read paths and entries 4 and 5 against a live chainId.

acceptance.clause: The suite passes in the gate on a clean checkout, fails when one planted rule break is introduced in any one module, and its smoke mode runs read-only against 46630 without sending a transaction.

units.title: Full release-1 deploy on 46630 with smoke
units.description: Delivers CAP-28's "every contract is verified and public" on the final deployment: follows the deploy runbook to put the final release-1 contracts on 46630 through Ignition, verify every one on Blockscout, wire the timelock, Safe and one role per key, regenerate the chain module, point the Vercel production app and Render worker at it, fund the role keys, faucet and Gas Manager policy, and run entry 13's smoke mode and the entry 4 and 5 checks against it.
units.unknown: Is the final deployment a fresh deploy of every contract (recommended: clean state, proves the deploy runbook) or the epics' incrementally upgraded deployment, and if fresh, which live schema does the worker index into, given no destructive SQL on game without the owner?

acceptance.clause: The entry 4 and 5 launch checks and the entry 13 smoke mode all pass against the final 46630 deployment, and a fresh email login on the Vercel production URL hatches a pet and sees it indexed.

units.title: Launch checklist passes and the owner opens testnet to players
units.description: Delivers CAP-28 and the "ships all at once" constraint at opening: writes the launch checklist in epic-launch/ with every epic's Done when item checked on the final deployment with its evidence (tx hash, screen, report), runs the manual phone and desktop pass for what the suite cannot see (3D pets, onboarding, Empty/Loading/Error/Offline states, push and Telegram), and records the owner's OK to open, after which the success-signal and counter-metric counting starts.

acceptance.clause: The launch checklist shows every epic's Done when item ticked with evidence on the final deployment and the owner's dated OK, and the ops dashboard shows MetricDaily rows starting from the opening day.
